text:
maria: heads up — AcmeAI reported a sudden spike in 5xx/504s hitting hosted inference around 11:12am PT during their campaign. ~18% error rate.
kevin: bringing eng-sre in. Any deploys or infra changes?
deploy-bot: deploy 'inference-service' revision v2.14.3 rolled to cluster-us-east1 @ 2026-03-15T18:09:10Z.
raj: grabbing metrics — gateway queue depth jumped, average upstream latency for backend pool peaked at 28s.
tyler: do we have autoscaler state? KEDA ScaledObject looks like default minReplicaCount=0 for many tenant pools. Polling interval is 30s. That's a long loop for sudden traffic.
maria: customer logs show gateway timeouts:
```
[2026-03-15T18:09:23Z] proxy_upstream_time=30012ms status=504 route=/v1/generate tenant=acme
[2026-03-15T18:09:24Z] error="no healthy upstreams"
```
kevin: i also see readinessProbe behavior: pods mark ready at container start, but model init (KV load) completes ~35-50s later. Pod receives traffic and OOMs/waits during that window.
tyler: also found sporadic registry auth 401 on image pulls for v2.14.3, ~35s worth of failures on a subset of nodes. Combine that with KEDA allowing scale-to-zero -> cold start chain.
raj: current infra snapshot:
```
ScaledObject inference-worker-so  pollingInterval: 30s  cooldownPeriod: 300s  minReplicaCount: 0
HPA inference-worker-hpa  min=1 max=40 metrics: cpu target 60%  currentReplicas=1
```
maria: so KEDA can scale to 0 despite HPA presence? that race creates a window where no pods available and then long delays to spin up.
tyler: yes. quick mitigation ideas: 1) set minReplicaCount >=2 for Acme tenant; 2) reduce pollingInterval to 5s; 3) change readinessProbe to verify model-ready flag; 4) add image-pull retry/backoff for registry auth.
kevin: applying a hot patch: `kubectl patch scaledobject inference-worker-so -n hosted --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":2,"pollingInterval":5}}'`
raj: i'm also opening a tiny admission webhook rule to block minReplicaCount=0 for inference ScaledObjects in prod — will push as config patch.
maria: customer wants repro steps and ETA. kevin, how long for hot patch and new pods?
kevin: patch applied. KEDA poll should pick up within ~5s; new pods scheduling depends on image pull. If image pulls succeed, ~45-70s to be fully ready because model init. ETA ~2-3m to see error rate drop.
tyler: repro steps I ran in staging to mirror failures:
1) set ScaledObject minReplicaCount=0 and pollingInterval=30s
2) deploy a model image with postStart sleep 45s to simulate long init
3) fire a sudden load: `hey -z 20s -c 40 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
Observe gateway 504s and backlog, then HPA/KEDA slow reaction.
raj: load test command used above in staging. I also forwarded kube events showing `ErrImagePull` and then `Back-off pulling image` during the window.
maria: customer asked whether we can offer a short-term reserved warm pool for paid tenants.
tyler: short-term policy: reserve 2 warm pods for customers flagged as "priority" during high traffic dates. Ops can flip a flag in tenant config. Long-term we need better defaults.\e support-bot: incident ticket #INC-20260315-347 created and linked to customer case.
kevin: additional quick fix — change readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds to 40 and add a `/model-ready` endpoint that returns success only after KV cache load. I'll cut a tiny sidecar that exposes the flag if the app can't.
raj: follow-up items for backlog/epic: - reconcile KEDA/HPA so ScaledObjects can't scale to 0 when HPA exists - default ScaledObject template minReplicaCount=1 and pollingInterval=10s for inference - add image registry auth retry and diagnostics - implement warmup endpoint and tenant warm pool toggle
tyler: saving reproducer harness and collected logs under /incidents/acme-autoscale-2026-03-15. I'll attach to the ticket.
maria: customer reported error rate dropped to ~4% after the patch. they asked for postmortem. I'll draft and assign owners for the epic items.
kevin: marking this as mitigated for now. keeping ticket open for the follow-ups.
raj: note — we should also add a runbook step: when customer sees sudden 5xx spike, check ScaledObject minReplicaCount and pollingInterval first, then check image pull events.
maria: thanks all. closing the immediate loop with Acme. will schedule postmortem and link to runbook updates. :white_check_mark:
